### Spatial Neighbors Calculation

::::: {.arg-table role="table"}
:::: {.arg-row .arg-head role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="columnheader"}
Name
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="columnheader"}
Description
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="columnheader"}
Attributes
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--coord_type`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Type of coordinate system. Valid options are:
`grid` - grid coordinates. Only relevant for lattice-based layouts (e.g. Visium). Builds a graph assuming a regular grid topology, where neighbors aredefined by grid adjacency rather than distance.
`generic` - Generic coordinates. Recommended for imaging-based data. This option is appropriate for irregularly spaced points, such as cell centroids or spot coordinates from imaging-based assays (e.g. Xenium, CosMx). Setting this option avoids grid-assumption artifacts and ensures each node has spatial neighbors as defined by distance.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`string`

[Default]{.arg-key} `"generic"`

[Choices]{.arg-key} `"generic"`, `"grid"`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--n_spatial_neighbors`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Depending on `--coord_type`:
`grid` - number of neighboring tiles.
`generic` - number of neighborhoods for non-grid data. Only used when `--delaunay False`.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`integer`

[Default]{.arg-key} `6`

[Min]{.arg-key} `1`
:::
::::
:::: {.arg-row role="row"}
::: {.arg-name role="cell"}
`--delaunay`
:::
::: {.arg-desc role="cell"}
Whether to use Delaunay triangulation to determine spatial neighborhood graph.
Only used when `--coord_type generic`.
:::
::: {.arg-attrs role="cell"}
`boolean`

[Default]{.arg-key} `false`
:::
::::
:::::

## Example commands

You can run the pipeline using `nextflow run`.

### View help

You can use `--help` as a parameter to get an overview of the possible parameters.

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline_spatial \
  -r v0.7.0 -latest \
  -main-script target/nextflow/neighbors/spatial_neighborhood_graph/main.nf \
  --help
```

### Run command

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Create a params.yaml"}
The command below reads this component's arguments from a `params.yaml` file. To create one:

- generate it with the form on [Viash Hub](https://www.viash-hub.com/packages/openpipeline_spatial/v0.7.0/components/neighbors/spatial_neighborhood_graph);
- see examples of using params files in the [guides](/guides/index.qmd);
- run several samples in one go with a [`param_list`](/guides/process-many-samples.qmd).
:::

Run locally with:

```bash
nextflow run openpipelines-bio/openpipeline_spatial \
  -r v0.7.0 -latest \
  -profile docker \
  -main-script target/nextflow/neighbors/spatial_neighborhood_graph/main.nf \
  -params-file params.yaml
```

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Other backends and platforms"}
Replace `-profile docker` with `-profile podman` or `-profile singularity` depending on the desired backend. To run on Seqera Platform or through Viash Hub, see the [guides](/guides/index.qmd).
:::
